title: Integration discovery - Cirrus Commerce
next_steps: Sofia to send Dedicated SKU + pricing by 2026-08-21
Arjun to share LangChain/LlamaIndex integration example repo by 2026-08-20
Schedule 2-hour benchmark session with Cirrus infra team week of 2026-08-24
action_items: Sofia: send pricing & dedicated capacity SKUs (due 2026-08-21)
Arjun: share LangChain + LlamaIndex quickstart repo and sample prompts (due 2026-08-20)
Priya / Cirrus: provide sample traffic shape and max RPS per region before benchmark (due 2026-08-22)
summary: Discovery call to understand Cirrus Commerce integration needs for payment-chat & order-support features. Discussed SDK/agent integrations (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits, observability hooks, and hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: share integration examples, send pricing SKUs, schedule benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Redwood - Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia with Redwood Inference, AE on this account. We have Arjun our solutions engineer. Can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Customer - Maya: Sure, I'm Maya Lopez, CTO at Cirrus. We run customer support chat and order routing, scaling globally.
[00:20] Customer - Ben: Ben Carter, lead ML eng, I own infra for models and the LLM features.
[00:26] Customer - Priya: Priya Singh, platform engineer, I own API gateway and auth.
[00:32] Redwood - Arjun: Quick wave, I'm Arjun, I focus on integrations and perf.
[00:38] Redwood - Sofia: Goal today is to understand your integration path 	6 SDKs, LangChain or LlamaIndex usage, whether you need Hosted for fast time-to-market, Dedicated for predictable throughput, or Private (VPC) for compliance.
[00:50] Customer - Maya: High level 	6 we have an existing agent architecture built on LangChain, some LlamaIndex for vector search. Right now calls go to provider X 	6 cost and latency are creeping up. We want to evaluate Redwood for lower per-token cost and better on-prem options.
[01:06] Customer - Ben: Our main workloads: chat for support (short sessions, strict latency), and nightly reranking/embeddings jobs. Peak is about 350 RPS for chat across us-east/us-west-eu with a p95 latency goal of ~120ms.
[01:26] Redwood - Arjun: Nice. A couple of clarifying Qs 	6 is the LangChain stack running server-side agents or inside user browsers? Also, are you using LlamaIndex for offline indexing only or at query time?
[01:36] Customer - Ben: Server-side. LlamaIndex is mostly at query time for retrieval augmented responses.
[01:44] Redwood - Sofia: Do you have compliance constraints 	6 SOC2, specific data residency, KMS?
[01:49] Customer - Maya: SOC 2 is a must, and some EU customers require data residency in eu-west-1. Eventually we might want customer-managed KMS for Private.
[01:58] Redwood - Arjun: We support SOC2, can do region pinning, and Private deployments offer customer KMS integrations. For hosted, we provide audit logs and retention controls 	6 might be enough for many customers.
[02:12] Customer - Priya: On the integration side 	6 we have an API gateway that fronts all third-party LLM calls, we need a simple SDK or HTTP path we can plug in. Also we use OpenTelemetry for traces.
[02:22] Redwood - Arjun: Good, we have native SDKs for Node/Python and a REST API. We also provide middleware examples for common gateways and a sample LangChain connector that you can drop into your agents. We emit spans compatible with OpenTelemetry and have per-request metadata hooks.
[02:40] Customer - Maya: Can you show the LangChain example, like how it handles streaming responses and function calling?
[02:46] Redwood - Arjun: Sure, TL;DR 	6 our SDK supports streaming via event streams and chunked responses. LangChain integrations use the standard LLM interface; we added an optional streaming iterator. For function calls we map Redwood tool-calling to LangChain tool output 	6 some small adapter glue. We'll share a repo after this.
[03:06] Customer - Ben: Are there known issues with LlamaIndex vector store performance on your hosted infra? We rely on fast retrieval.
[03:14] Redwood - Arjun: LlamaIndex itself is client-side; embeddings and vector stores are your infra. For embeddings we provide efficient batch endpoints and embedding models optimized for throughput. If you push embedding compute to us, we can give batching recommendations. If you self-host vector store, we typically recommend prefix caching and key-value cache for repeated contexts to reduce token consumption.
[03:35] Customer - Ben: Prefix caching 	6 do you mean Redwood's KV cache on the serving side?
[03:39] Redwood - Arjun: Yes, we have KV cache options in the runtime 	6 sometimes transcribed as K-V cash 	6 which store repeated prefixes or retrieved context to avoid re-sending tokens. It's configurable per-route.
[03:50] Customer - Priya: About gateway/proxy: we currently have rate limiting at the gateway. If we route to Redwood hosted, do we still keep the gateway or route direct?
[03:59] Redwood - Sofia: Many customers keep the gateway as single control plane for auth/quota. You can route gateway->Redwood API with per-route keys. Alternatively Dedicated or Private can be deployed behind your VPC so calls never leave your network.
[04:14] Customer - Priya: What's the pattern for ephemeral keys and quotas? We often want per-tenant quotas.
[04:19] Redwood - Arjun: Two common patterns: 1) Gateway mints short-lived Redwood API keys per tenant and proxies requests, enforcing quotas at gateway level; or 2) Gateway maps tenant->Redwood route and we configure per-route quotas on Redwood side (more precise billing). We can support both.
[04:36] Customer - Maya: Latency concerns 	6 hosted vs dedicated. At peak we need 120ms p95. Is that realistic with streaming?
[04:44] Redwood - Arjun: For short-turn chat that tight, Dedicated pools with pinned GPU capacity are the safest to hit 120ms p95. Hosted works for many customers but depends on burst patterns and model choice. We can run a benchmark to validate.
[04:58] Customer - Ben: What about model variants 	6 do you do automated fallback if capacity constrained?
[05:03] Redwood - Arjun: Yes, smart routing policies 	6 fall back to compatible quantized variants or regional replicas. You can define policy by latency, cost, or version pinning.
[05:14] Customer - Priya: Observability 	6 what hooks do you expose for our telemetry/alerts?
[05:18] Redwood - Arjun: We provide per-request metadata, trace IDs, token-level cost breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. You can export traces to a collector or pull logs via API. We also expose webhooks for error alerts and quality regression events.
[05:34] Customer - Maya: On security, will you provide SOC 2 + SAML SSO for the console?
[05:39] Redwood - Sofia: Yes, SAML/SSO + RBAC in the console. For Private we support enterprise SSO integration and optional audit-forwarding.
[05:49] Customer - Ben: Does Redwood support model compilation/quantization on dedicated infra? We want lower cost on embeddings jobs.
[05:56] Redwood - Arjun: The runtime picks kernels and supports quantized execution paths. For embeddings jobs you can schedule on cheaper SKU pools or use batch endpoints with aggressive batching to lower per-unit cost.
[06:10] Customer - Priya: Can we run a POC where we push production traffic for a week on a Dedicated pool?
[06:16] Redwood - Sofia: Yes, typical POC flows: short pilot with a dedicated pool or hosted with reserved capacity. We'll propose a pilot scope in the follow-up.
[06:24] Customer - Maya: For data residency, we need eu-west-1 hosting for EU customers. Any blockers?
[06:29] Redwood - Arjun: We have region pinning and can host dedicated capacity in EU region. For Private, you can deploy on-prem or in your VPC subnets.
[06:39] Customer - Ben: About quotas 	6 we have spikes to 900 RPS on Black Friday. How does autoscaling / burst work?
[06:46] Redwood - Arjun: Autoscaling policies are configurable with burst capacity options. Dedicated pools can have buffer headroom and autoscale thresholds. For extreme spikes, recommended pattern is hybrid: keep critical latency traffic on Dedicated and route overflow to hosted variants with graceful degradation policies.
[07:05] Customer - Priya: Any constraints with our gateway TLS termination? Our gateway does TLS and gRPC to internal services.
[07:12] Redwood - Arjun: Our endpoints accept TLS and gRPC. If you want a private deployment behind your gateway, we support mTLS for mutual auth.
[07:21] Customer - Maya: We use LlamaIndex for retrieval. Any special considerations for embeddings model selection?
[07:27] Redwood - Arjun: Choose embeddings that match embedding dimensionality expectations of your vector store. We provide batched embeddings and will show cost/throughput tradeoffs. Also recommend local caching of embeddings when stable.
[07:39] Customer - Ben: How do you charge for caching 	6 is it per-token or per-request?
[07:43] Redwood - Sofia: Billing typically counts tokens generated and embeddings units. Caching reduces token usage but storage for cached objects isn't billed as tokens; there may be storage/retention tiers. We'll include billing details in the SKU doc.
[07:58] Customer - Priya: Observability again 	6 we want correlation IDs to tie calls to our logs.
[08:03] Redwood - Arjun: We can accept your correlation ID header and surface it in logs and traces. We recommend passing a request_id that flows through.
[08:11] Customer - Maya: Any SDK gotchas with streaming + LangChain async chains?
[08:16] Redwood - Arjun: A couple: ensure your chain's timeouts align with streaming windows, and the LangChain adapter can emit tokens as they arrive. We'll share an example using asyncio and stream iterators.
[08:29] Customer - Ben: For the benchmark 	6 we'll want to replicate our traffic shape with 95th percentile session lengths. I'll compile a traffic shape and sample prompts.
[08:36] Customer - Priya: We'll also want to test failure modes 	6 gateway downtime and fallback to hosted variants.
[08:41] Redwood - Sofia: Good call, we can design the benchmark with failure scenarios.
[08:45] Customer - Maya: What about rate limits per api key? We sometimes want per-tenant limit of 60rpm.
[08:51] Redwood - Arjun: We support per-key quotas; you can set per-route or per-tenant quotas and granular throttles. If you prefer gateway enforced quotas, that's fine too.
[08:59] Customer - Ben: Any sample CV or SLAs for Dedicated? Need expected p95 and uptime numbers.
[09:05] Redwood - Sofia: We'll attach the Dedicated SLA doc 	6 typical uptime 99.9% and latency SLOs dependent on model/variant. We'll include benchmark expectations in the pilot proposal.
[09:18] Customer - Maya: Can you send references of customers in payments/commerce?
[09:22] Redwood - Sofia: Yes, we'll include 2 anonymized references and a case study.
[09:27] Customer - Priya: One operational question 	6 rotation of API keys. How to rotate without dropping in-flight sessions?
[09:33] Redwood - Arjun: We support key rotation with a grace period; clients can present either old or new keys during rotation window. For streaming, maintain the connection; new connections use the new key.
[09:44] Customer - Ben: Ok, that's helpful. Are rate limits measured per second or minute? We want bursty allowances.
[09:51] Redwood - Arjun: Both 	6 you can set per-second burst and a sustained per-minute rate, plus leaky-bucket policies.
[10:01] Customer - Maya: Anything else we should review?
[10:04] Redwood - Sofia: We'll follow up with: 1) Dedicated SKU + pricing, 2) LangChain/LlamaIndex quickstart repo, 3) benchmark proposal + times, 4) security docs (SOC2, ISO, SAML).
[10:16] Customer - Maya: Great, please include a rough estimate for cost delta vs our current provider.
[10:20] Redwood - Sofia: We'll include an estimate and assumptions.
[10:24] Customer - Ben: Timeline 	6 we want to pick a pilot by end of month.
[10:28] Redwood - Sofia: Sounds good. We'll aim to get proposals out in 48 hours.
[10:33] Redwood - Arjun: I'll share the LangChain adapter, streaming examples, and a small script to simulate the traffic shape.
[10:40] Customer - Priya: We'll send over sample traffic and the list of sensitive PII fields we redact.
[10:45] Redwood - Sofia: Perfect. Any final questions?
[10:48] Customer - Maya: No, that covers it. Thanks.
[10:50] Redwood - Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up.

[Transcript notes 	6 occasional transcription noise: 'K-V cash' appears at 03:35, 'LlamaIndex' sometimes transcribed as 'Lama Index' in internal notes, minor punctuation drops.]
